rationale:
structural: The structural obligations are: (1) a public `sources::StructuralRule` type with private fields and the listed signatures (`languages`, `compile`, `extensions`, `matches`); (2) `SourceProject::search_structure` "uses the same matcher for project files". The other clauses (error reporting, extensions non-empty, distinct ordered spans) are observable behavior.

The code supports both obligations. In `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs`, `struct[StructuralRule]` has a single private field `inner`. `impl[StructuralRule]` declares `languages() -> Vec<&'static str>`, `compile(&str, &Map<String, Value>) -> Result<Self, SourceError>`, `extensions(&self) -> &[&str]` and `matches(&self, &str) -> Vec<Span>`. These match the prescribed signatures. `compile` maps errors to `SourceError::Invalid`. `languages` delegates to `QueryLanguage::names()`. `extensions` delegates to the language profile's extensions. `matches` converts the inner byte ranges to `Span`.

In `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/hits.rs`, `impl[SourceProject<D>]/fn[search_structure]` compiles a `StructuralRule` with `StructuralRule::compile` and passes `rule.matches(text)` as the matcher to `find_hits`. That is the same public rule type and matcher used for project files. An alternative that used a different matcher for project files would violate the clause, and this code does not do that.

Both supplied roots carry `{impl}` markers and cover these obligations. No further roots are needed.

behavioral: I found no test-adequacy gap. I did not need to read implementation source.

- **`languages` and `compile` agree.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/structural.rs#mod[tests]/fn[rules_compile_for_every_grammar_and_report_invalid_input]` compiles a rule for each of 8 languages, searches sample text, and asserts the matched text. It then asserts `tested == StructuralRule::languages()`, so every listed language is accepted and the list has no untested entry.
- **Compile errors.** The same test checks that unknown languages (`cobol`, `plain-text`) fail with "unknown structural search language". It also checks a missing `rule` key, an unexpected `fix` key, a nonexistent node kind and a bogus rule key. Each is asserted on the error message. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/search.rs#fn[compile_once_and_search_supplied_source]` asserts `SourceError::Invalid` for an unknown language and for an empty core. Compilation takes no source, so this covers "even when there is no source to search".
- **`extensions`.** For every grammar, the first test asserts that the list is non-empty, that no entry is empty and that none starts with a dot. `compile_once_and_search_supplied_source` asserts that Rust includes `rs`.
- **Distinct spans.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/search.rs#fn[nodes_covering_the_same_source_produce_one_span]` matches `source_file`, `function_item` and both together over identical bytes. Each case asserts exactly one `Span`.
- **Order by start, then end.** `compile_once_and_search_supplied_source` asserts `["f(g())","g()","h()"]`. It also asserts `["f()","f()()"]`, where two spans share a start. A tree walk would visit the outer node first, so this case checks the end tiebreak.
- **Offsets refer to the input on each call.** The test reuses one compiled rule over three different texts. One text contains `é`, so byte offsets are checked against slices of that input. The empty string returns no matches.
- **`SourceProject::search_structure` uses the same matcher.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_tags_select_only_the_original_enclosing_item]` compiles a `StructuralRule` and asserts that `rule.matches` on the file text equals the spans returned by `tools.search_structure`.

text: A `sources::StructuralRule` is a structural query compiled for repeated searches
of text supplied by the caller. `languages` lists the bundled grammar names
accepted by `compile`. Compilation reports an unknown language or an invalid
ast-grep rule core, even when there is no source to search. `extensions` lists
the language's filename extensions without leading dots and contains at least one entry.
`matches` searches the supplied UTF-8 text and returns distinct half-open byte
spans ordered by start, then end. Offsets refer to that input on each call.
`SourceProject::search_structure` uses the same matcher for project files.
